aesthetics.title: \text{Six spine basis terms}
aesthetics.description: Take t=mean(x). The first four terms are the unbounded cubic Hermite basis h00,h01,h10,h11. The last two are T2(z) and T3(z), with z=tanh((softplus(a)+1e-4)*(t+0.5*tanh(b))).

aesthetics.title: \text{Coordinate edge factor}
aesthetics.description: Warp each input coordinate with a second learned scale and shift. Evaluate T0,T1,T2,T3 and contract their four coefficients separately for each input/output coordinate pair. These weights are not shared between input coordinates.

aesthetics.title: \text{Original KS2 damping}
aesthetics.description: Let total=sum(x), t=mean(x), delta=x-t. Use w=x/total unless abs(total)<1e-6, when w=1/K. Both damping strengths use softplus. This is the original ks2.py denominator, not the stabilized variant.

aesthetics.title: \text{Damp each edge}
aesthetics.description: Elementwise division before reducing input coordinates.

aesthetics.title: \text{KS2: spine and damped factorized edges}
aesthetics.description: Standalone KS2 maps K input coordinates directly to N outputs. C_spine has shape [6,N], C_t [6,K,N], and C_x [4,K,N]. The spine and longitudinal edge factor share Phi and its warp. There is no projection, coordinate bypass, ReLU or iteration.
